conventions.convention: Mathematical flows use U(t)=exp(itT); physical evolution uses T=−H_op/ℏ, ℏ>0, hence U(t)=exp(−itH_op/ℏ).
The mathematical lemmas assume a nonzero complex Hilbert space and AC together with Countable Choice; the physical system additionally inherits the nonzero separable Hilbert-space assignment of P1.
Norm differentiation of U(t)x holds exactly for x∈D(T), at every time; outside D(T) the orbit is nowhere norm-differentiable. The Heisenberg equation additionally requires bounded A with A D(T)⊆D(T).

Stationarity of a pure preparation means invariance of its ray for every real time, rather than equality of its representing vectors. Energy compatibility means commutation of all spectral projections, rather than a formal commutator on a smaller domain.
Pure-ray probabilities use a unit representative; raw first and second moment formulas for a nonzero representative are divided by its squared norm.
The two-level pairing is linear in its first argument. Y=iT_(u2,u1)−iT_(u1,u2), ω=(E2−E1)/ℏ, and the expectation triple rotates by R3(−ωt). Energies are declared model parameters in joules.
Return times are positive and refer to the ray. Phase comparisons involve only S={n:c_n≠0}; repeated eigenvalues and singleton support are allowed.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC and Countable Choice, for a self-adjoint T on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, U(t)=exp(itT) is a strongly continuous unitary group, preserves D(T), commutes with T there and with every bounded Borel function of T; U(t)x is differentiable everywhere exactly when x∈D(T), with derivative iTU(t)x, and otherwise nowhere differentiable.

Under P1, P2 and P4, fixes the assigned self-adjoint energy observable and unit, U(t)=exp(−itH_op/ℏ), vector and density evolution, bounded Heisenberg representatives, stationary preparations, eigenstates and strong spectral energy compatibility.

For the declared isolated-system energy observable under P1, P2, P4 and the choice hypotheses, the flow is unitary, preserves the energy domain, satisfies iℏψ′=H_opψ exactly for domain initial vectors, and transports density preparations by unitary conjugation; tr(ρ(t)B)=tr(ρ(0)U(t)*BU(t)) for bounded B.

For bounded A, A(t)=U(−t)AU(t) preserves norm and adjoints and is strongly continuous and covariant. If A D(T)⊆D(T), then A(t)x is differentiable for x∈D(T), with derivative −i[T,A(t)]x. For self-adjoint A, its spectral PVM is transported by conjugation and its spectrum is unchanged.
For nonzero ψ and self-adjoint T under the stated choice hypotheses, U(t)ψ∈Cψ for every real t if and only if ψ∈D(T) and Tψ=λψ for some real λ; then U(t)ψ=exp(itλ)ψ.

Under the declared autonomous model, every preparation has a conserved energy law; nonzero pure representatives in D(H_op) have finite conserved first and second energy moments with normalized formulas; bounded energy-compatible sharp observables have conserved laws; stationary pure preparations are exactly energy eigenrays, and every sharp-observable law is constant in such a preparation.
For the declared two-level model with E1≠E2, computes the exact spectral flow, X,Y,Z means and R3(−ωt) rotation, conserved energy weights, and μ_X({+1})=(1+cos(ωt))/2 in the equal-weight preparation.

concerns.concern: F5 says 'for the bounded case the representing integral is Φ_E(id)'. The cited bounded integral takes bounded functions on R, whereas id:R→R is unbounded even when the represented operator is bounded. Use the unbounded PVM integral or an explicitly bounded function agreeing with id on the spectral support. Spectral uniqueness and step 3.2 remain valid.

Clause (vi) covers 'every assigned sharp observable', but verification 3.3 explicitly proves the conclusion only for 'every bounded assigned sharp observable' and then says 'This is (vi)'. The same-ray argument applies to every spectral projection, including those of an unbounded observable, so the missing extension is immediate.
Verification 4.1 says 'its norm is 4r²+(|α|²−|β|²)²=...=1'. That calculation gives the squared Euclidean norm; taking its nonnegative square root proves the stated norm-one conclusion.

alerts.finding: F5 says 'a positive measure with μ(R\{λ})=0 is the point mass at λ'. Support at one point gives μ=μ({λ})δ_λ, with no unit-mass conclusion unless normalization is assumed. For example 2δ_λ satisfies the displayed support condition. Step 6.1 uses a unit vector, so its actual scalar measure has mass one; clarify the general fact's normalization.

Definition (f) says 'The parameter a of a translation has the unit of length u_H'. The autonomous-evolution supplier defines u_H as the energy unit of H_op, while the quantities supplier assigns translation parameters metres. The symbol is inconsistent with the cited energy interface.

Definition (a) says AC 'is assumed only in the Coulomb realization of clause (d)(ii)', but (e) invokes the assigned-observable spectral law and autonomous flow of suppliers whose Definitions explicitly assume AC in all realizations. The Countable-Choice-only bounded spatial branch needs an exact alternative supplier or a local construction, or the imported choice hypothesis must be carried. Finite-dimensional special cases can be justified directly.

Definition (e) calls the autonomous family exp(−itH_LM/ℏ) 'the reading of clause (iv) of P4'. P4(ii) supplies autonomous evolution; P4(iv) instead discusses prescribed time-dependent families as a different model assumption. The clause locator is incorrect.

seams_checked.note: Assigned self-adjoint pairs, spectral Born laws and domain-qualified moments retain the supplier's units, normalization and choice hypotheses.
P1, P2 and autonomous P4 are adopted assumptions; the negative energy-flow sign, explicit ℏ and SI dimensions agree.
Nonzero rays, unit representatives and positive trace-one density preparations are used consistently.
Density expansions and trace cyclicity are used with trace-class inputs and bounded multipliers; no unbounded trace permutation is claimed.

Conserved-law clauses are instantiated with a self-adjoint energy, strong spectral compatibility and domain-qualified moments. The external F5 wording concern does not invalidate the normalized eigenvector use.
Energy parameters are in joules, phases are dimensionless and ω has inverse-second units; calculated parameters are not reported measurements.
Probabilities use spectral projections and normalized representatives; bounded example means have the required integrability.
Ray return, phase equivalence, normalized rank-one states and exclusion of the zero vector agree with the supplier.
Rank-one operators use the linear-first convention; their adjoints, projections and finite products agree with the supplied calculus.
The eigenvector phase formula and conserved energy probabilities are used within their hypotheses.
Translation and boost covariance invoke self-adjoint bounded-potential flows with norm equations restricted to the declared Sobolev domain.
The local continuity theorem separately assumes a regular differential solution; global P4 norm conservation is used independently and does not assert that every orbit has a smooth representative.
The energy-time caveat retains parameter time and explicitly requires bounded A preserving the energy domain for its Heisenberg identification.
The energy-flow and stationary-state citations retain nonzero representatives, domain conditions and division by squared norm for moments.
The separately realized self-adjoint oscillator supplies its own energy domain; autonomous spectral flow is applied to that realization.
Flow, domain and preparation citations agree, but the symmetry definition's clause (f) reuses the energy-unit symbol u_H as a length unit; alerted to its owner.
Free, parity and central-potential examples use the declared self-adjoint bounded-potential model and autonomous flow; stronger conservation results come from the symmetry suppliers.
Autonomous evolution is invoked after self-adjointness of the relevant free or Zeeman operator is supplied; unbounded angular conservation is established by separate symmetry results.
Zeeman spectral flow and spin-sector norm preservation retain their separately supplied operator and domain hypotheses.
Coulomb self-adjoint realization precedes the flow reading; stationary rays and eigenvector phases agree with the cited characterization.
Variational and perturbed-family definitions adopt the energy-observable vocabulary without claiming that autonomous evolution supplies approximation controls.
Driven evolution is explicitly a separate model assumption. The autonomous supplier supplies only the free-flow factor; bounded interaction-picture PVM conjugation uses the exact Heisenberg lemma.
Free, short-range and Coulomb comparison flows are tied to their separately established self-adjoint energy realizations; autonomous dynamics is not cited as proving scattering completeness.
Evolution and eigenray formulas agree, but the fixed-N definition limits AC to its Coulomb branch while citing the general AC-assuming spectral and evolution interfaces in every realization.
The two-site hypothetical scenario uses the exact two-point spectral phases of its declared finite Hamiltonian and keeps model arithmetic distinct from data.

The coupled-model definition cites P4(iv) for an autonomous flow; the correct clause is P4(ii). Its nonzero-dimensional flow formula otherwise agrees, and the zero-dimensional branch is handled separately.
